title: Shadow-band staffing rotations and decision lattice for mid-cycle scope cuts
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Problem: During mid-cycle shocks (urgent incidents, large unplanned infra work, or a critical sales request) we repeatedly end up making ad-hoc scope cuts without consistent, documented rationale. That causes cross-team confusion, uneven customer impact, and hidden technical debt.

Proposal: Create a lightweight operational runbook — the 'shadow-band' rotation model — that pairs a small, rotating pool of cross-functional engineers and a product shadow to own short-notice capacity decisions for two-week windows. Pair this rotation with a compact decision lattice (quantitative thresholds + qualitative guardrails) to drive consistent scope-trim choices.

Components: 1) Shadow-band roster and onboarding checklist (roles: capacity owner, QA lead, customer liaison); 2) Decision lattice with numeric thresholds (SLO violation %, request queue growth rate, critical customer SLA risk) and mapped cut tiers (A: non-customer-facing nice-to-have -> immediate trim; B: optimization tasks -> delay; C: security/compliance -> escalate not cut); 3) Communication templates (status banner, PR labels, changelog entry); 4) Post-mortem and re-instatement flow for cut items.

Why this is different: Instead of relying on only exec-level triage, the shadow-band formalizes a rapid operational layer so decisions can be made close to the work with documented trade-offs and an auditable trail. It ties staffing (temporary reallocation) to scope decisions and clarifies re-onboarding steps for deferred items.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Shadow-band roster template (Google Sheet) created and adopted by at least 3 teams. 2) Decision lattice doc published in Confluence and referenced in the cycle handbook. 3) Two simulated mid-cycle exercises run with end-to-end timing tracked (<= 48h from trigger to posted decision). 4) All cut items logged in a triage backlog with re-onboarding checklist. 5) Stakeholder signoff from Eng PM, Head of Reliability, and Design.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish playbook draft and roster template. Week 1: Recruit volunteers and shadow pairings; run a tabletop exercise with 3 mock incidents. Week 2: Soft launch on one product squad (observe, collect timing and conflict points). Week 3: Adjust thresholds and comms; expand to two more squads. Ongoing: quarterly drills and retro. Emergency escalation path: if decision lattice yields 'escalate' then engage Exec on-call within 4 hours.
metrics: Operational metrics to track: 1) Decision latency (trigger->decision) target <48h. 2) % of cut items with documented customer impact and re-onboard plan target 100%. 3) Number of scope cuts reversed due to missing context (target 0 after 2 cycles). 4) Measured customer impact (support tickets and SLA violations) before/after. 5) Shadow-band load (FTE-equivalent hours/week).

2025-11-13 Marco Diaz: Ran a tabletop exercise with infra and payments teams. Time to decision: 28h. Observations: ambiguity at owner handoff and ambiguity in 'optimization' vs 'feature' categorization. Next step: add example-based taxonomy to lattice.

2025-11-15 Leah Chen: Updated Confluence doc with example taxonomy and two sample incidents. Created follow-up sub-issue PM-193848 to track automation of roster notifications and escalation page. Requesting formal signoffs by 2025-11-20.
2025-11-17 Hannah Sato (Support): Confirmed template covers support communication needs. Raised a minor ask to add a 'customer outreach owner' field on the roster sheet.
